pharm: Glycopeptide antibiotic active against Gram-positive organisms including MRSA and enterococci; long half-life allowing once-daily dosing after a loading phase; IM or IV (and oral for C. difficile).
quick: Loading 400 mg (or 6 mg/kg) q12h x3-5 doses, then 6 mg/kg once daily
N/A (parenteral); oral solution for C. diff
Avoid unless clearly necessary; limited data
Reduce maintenance dose/interval from day 4 by CrCl
Trough levels, renal function, FBC, hearing
summary: Teicoplanin is a glycopeptide antibiotic for serious Gram-positive infections, including MRSA, used much like vancomycin but with a long half-life permitting once-daily dosing (after a loading regimen) and giving by IM as well as IV. It is given orally only for Clostridioides difficile colitis (not systemically absorbed). It causes less of the histamine 'red-man' infusion reaction than vancomycin. It requires renal dose adjustment from day 4 and may cause nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, thrombocytopenia, and hypersensitivity. It is approved in Europe and many countries but is NOT FDA-approved.
indications: Serious Gram-positive infections, including those due to methicillin-resistant staphylococci (MRSA), where other antibiotics cannot be used
Bacteremia associated with the above infections
Peritonitis associated with continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD)
Oral: Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea/colitis (not systemically absorbed)

dosage.c: Moderate infections (skin/soft tissue, UTI, lower respiratory) - adults
dosage.d: Loading 400 mg (~6 mg/kg) every 12 h for 3 doses, then maintenance 400 mg (6 mg/kg) once daily
dosage.n: EMA/SmPC; weight-based 6 mg/kg used for accuracy

dosage.c: Severe infections (bone/joint, endocarditis, severe MRSA) - adults
dosage.d: Loading 12 mg/kg every 12 h for 3-5 doses, then 12 mg/kg once daily
dosage.n: Higher target troughs for deep-seated infection

dosage.d: Loading 10 mg/kg every 12 h for 3 doses, then 6-10 mg/kg once daily
dosage.n: Neonates: 16 mg/kg loading then 8 mg/kg once daily

dosage.d: 20 mg/L in each dialysis bag (after an IV loading dose)
Reduce maintenance dose or extend interval by CrCl
dosage.n: Mild-moderate: halve dose or give alternate days; severe/dialysis: further reduction, guided by levels

admin: Loading doses are essential because of the long half-life - do not give once-daily dosing from the outset
May be given by IV bolus (3-5 min) or IV infusion (30 min), or by intramuscular injection
Oral solution is reserved for C. difficile infection (not absorbed systemically)
Reconstitute carefully, avoiding foaming; inspect for particulate matter
Reduce maintenance dose in renal impairment starting from the fourth day of therapy
Monitor renal function and, in prolonged or high-dose therapy, serum trough levels and hearing
moa: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of peptidoglycan precursors, blocking cross-linking (transglycosylation/transpeptidation). This is bactericidal against susceptible aerobic and anaerobic Gram-positive bacteria, including methicillin-resistant staphylococci.

relative: Known hypersensitivity to vancomycin (cross-reactivity possible, not absolute)

preg: Limited human data; animal studies have shown some toxicity at high doses. Avoid during pregnancy unless clearly necessary (potential risk of inner-ear/renal effects).
lact: It is not known whether teicoplanin is excreted in human milk; a decision to discontinue breastfeeding or the drug should weigh benefit to mother and infant.
renal: Renal excretion is the main route. Reduce the maintenance dose (or extend the interval) starting from the fourth day of therapy based on creatinine clearance - in moderate impairment halve the daily dose or give it on alternate days; in severe impairment/dialysis reduce further, guided by trough levels. Teicoplanin is not significantly removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for hepatic impairment.

major: Other nephrotoxic/ototoxic agents (aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, ciclosporin, cisplatin, loop diuretics) - additive toxicity
moderate: Concurrent vancomycin (cross-hypersensitivity; do not substitute if a patient had red-man syndrome alone - that is not a true allergy)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum trough concentrations (target >=10 mg/L for most infections; >=15-30 mg/L for endocarditis/deep infection), renal function, and full blood count.

serious: Thrombocytopenia and other blood dyscrasias (neutropenia, eosinophilia)
emergency: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS

monitoring: Serum trough levels (target >=10 mg/L; >=15-30 mg/L for endocarditis and deep-seated infection)
Renal function (creatinine) before and during therapy, especially with nephrotoxic co-medication
Hearing/vestibular function in prolonged or high-dose therapy or with other ototoxic drugs
counsel: This antibiotic is given by injection (vein or muscle); the first few 'loading' doses are given closer together
Report rash, itching, fever, swelling, or breathing difficulty promptly
Tell the team about any kidney problems, hearing changes, or ringing in the ears
Complete the full course even if you feel better
pk: End of IV infusion; IM absorption ~90% bioavailable
Store below 25 C; reconstituted solution per labeling (refrigerate, use promptly)
pearls: Long half-life enables once-daily dosing, but loading doses are mandatory to reach therapeutic levels quickly
Causes far less of the histamine 'red-man' infusion reaction than vancomycin and can be given IM
Renal dose adjustment is delayed until the 4th day because of the long half-life
Not removed by hemodialysis - no supplemental post-dialysis dose needed
Oral teicoplanin treats C. difficile colitis and is not absorbed systemically
missed: Hospital-administered; if a maintenance dose is delayed, give it as soon as noted and resume once-daily dosing. Do not double the dose. The long half-life makes a single delayed dose unlikely to cause sub-therapeutic levels, but recheck troughs if timing changed significantly.
overdose: Manage symptomatically and supportively; there is no specific antidote. Teicoplanin is not effectively removed by hemodialysis (hemoperfusion may modestly increase clearance). Monitor renal function, blood counts, and hearing.
